questions.text: Who is the national hero of the Philippines?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Rizal, Jose Rizal.

questions.text: Which country colonized the Philippines after Spain?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: USA, America, Amerika.

questions.text: Which country occupied the Philippines during World War II?
On what date is Philippine Independence Day celebrated?
questions.hostNotes: Marks the 1898 proclamation of independence from Spain.

questions.text: Who was the first president of the Philippines?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Aguinaldo.

questions.text: Which Mactan chieftain defeated Ferdinand Magellan's forces in 1521?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Lapulapu, Cali Pulaco.

questions.text: Who founded the Katipunan in 1892?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Bonifacio, Andres Bonifacio. He co-founded it with others, but he is the accepted answer.

questions.text: The 1986 People Power Revolution is named after what major Metro Manila road?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Epifanio de los Santos Avenue.

questions.text: What is the title of José Rizal's first novel?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Noli. Not El Filibusterismo, which was his second.

questions.text: How many rays does the sun on the Philippine flag have?
questions.hostNotes: They stand for the first eight provinces to revolt against Spain.

questions.text: The Philippines was named after which future Spanish king?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Philip II, Felipe II. Must include "II" or "the Second".

questions.text: Which elderly woman, called the "Mother of the Katipunan", cared for wounded revolutionaries?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Tandang Sora.

questions.text: In which province did the 1942 Death March of Filipino and American prisoners begin?
Who sewed the first Philippine flag in Hong Kong?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Agoncillo. She was helped by her daughter Lorenza and Delfina Herbosa de Natividad.

questions.text: For about how many years did Spain rule the Philippines?
questions.hostNotes: Commonly taught as 333 years (1565 to 1898). Accept answers from 330 to 333.

questions.text: Who was the first female president of the Philippines?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Cory Aquino, Cory.

questions.text: Which American general vowed "I shall return" after leaving the Philippines in 1942?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: MacArthur. He landed in Leyte in 1944.

questions.text: Which president declared martial law in September 1972?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Marcos, Ferdinand E. Marcos Sr. It was done through Proclamation No. 1081.

questions.text: Who was the "Boy General" killed defending Tirad Pass in 1899?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Goyo, del Pilar. Not Marcelo H. del Pilar, the propagandist. He was 24.

questions.text: Which paralyzed hero is known as the "Brains of the Revolution"?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Mabini. Also called the "Sublime Paralytic".

questions.text: In which Cavite town was Philippine independence proclaimed in 1898?
questions.hostNotes: From the balcony of Aguinaldo's house, now the Aguinaldo Shrine.

questions.text: Who composed the music of the Philippine national anthem?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Julian Felipe.

questions.text: Who founded the first permanent Spanish settlement in the Philippines, in Cebu in 1565?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Legazpi, Legaspi. Not Magellan, who died in 1521.

questions.text: What combined name is given to the three Filipino priests executed by the Spanish in 1872?
questions.hostNotes: Fathers Mariano Gómez, José Burgos and Jacinto Zamora.

questions.text: What is the title of the farewell poem José Rizal wrote before his execution?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: My Last Farewell, Huling Paalam.

questions.text: Who was president of the Philippine Commonwealth when it was established in 1935?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Quezon.

questions.text: Whose assassination at the Manila International Airport in 1983 sparked mass protests?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Ninoy Aquino, Ninoy. The airport (NAIA) now bears his name.

questions.text: On what date in 1946 did the United States formally grant Philippine independence?
questions.hostNotes: Not June 12, Independence Day since 1962. July 4 is now observed as Philippine Republic Day.

questions.text: What newspaper of Filipino reformists was published in Spain starting in 1889?
What documents did Katipuneros tear up in the 1896 Cry of Pugad Lawin?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: cedula, sedula, community tax certificates. Some historians call the event the Cry of Balintawak.

questions.text: What precolonial Filipino script, now seen in logos and tattoos, uses symbols for syllables?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: alibata, though historians prefer baybayin.

questions.text: Who continued her husband Diego's revolt in Ilocos after his assassination in 1763?
What island fortress at the mouth of Manila Bay fell to Japan in May 1942?
The Manila galleons sailed across the Pacific to which Mexican port?
questions.hostNotes: The galleon trade ran from 1565 to 1815.

questions.text: Who became the first president of the independent Third Republic in 1946?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Roxas. Not Quezon or Osmeña, who led the Commonwealth.

questions.text: In which Bulacan church was the First Philippine Republic's constitution framed?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Barasoain. It is in Malolos, hence the Malolos Constitution.

questions.text: What 1897 truce sent the Filipino revolutionary leaders into exile in Hong Kong?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Biak-na-Bato.

questions.text: What Spanish-era system forced Filipino men to do 40 days of unpaid labor a year?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: polo, sapilitang paggawa. It was cut to 15 days in 1884.

questions.text: In the 1898 Treaty of Paris, how much did the United States pay Spain for the Philippines?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: 20 million dollars.

questions.text: Who led the longest revolt in Philippine history, lasting about 85 years in Bohol?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Dagohoy. The revolt ran from 1744 to 1829.

questions.text: What 1934 US law promised Philippine independence after a 10-year Commonwealth period?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Tydings-McDuffie, Philippine Independence Act. Not the Jones Law of 1916.

questions.text: Who wrote the "Kartilya ng Katipunan", the society's code of conduct?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Jacinto. He is called the "Brains of the Katipunan".

questions.text: What 17th-century Maguindanao sultan, now honored by a province's name, fought Spanish colonizers?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Kudarat, Muhammad Kudarat.

questions.text: What was the name of the Katipunan's newspaper, first published in 1896?
questions.hostNotes: Only one issue came out. Not La Solidaridad, which was the reformists' paper in Spain.

questions.text: What artifact dated 900 AD is the oldest known written document found in the Philippines?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Laguna Copperplate. It was found near Lumban, Laguna, in 1989.
